audit.why: full phases[N].side and content win[N] agree row for row and match the packet: Camille 1-3, Skill at 4-5, Master Yi at 6 and first item, Camille back at 2+ items.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike carries no cooldowns and mis-names her ult 'Hextech Ultimatum'.
audit.why: The real name is The Hextech Ultimatum, 140/115/90s. Highlander is a flat 85s, so at 6 you get roughly one and a half ults for each of hers — that is what makes the level 6 row yours.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text and spikes[2].text now carry the R and E timers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two false mechanics repeated across the content layer. (a) Tactical Sweep (W) is called a 'true-damage sweep' and a 'shield' — it is a delayed cone that damages, and in the outer half slows and HEALS Camille. The true damage in her kit is on Precision Protocol (Q). (b) 'True-damage shield' is written as her late-game answer to you. Adaptive Defenses shields against physical OR magic matched to the attacker, so Wuju Style's true damage passes straight through it.
audit.why: The page tells the player to fear a shield that cannot stop their main damage source and to ignore the heal that actually can.
audit.corrected: W Tactical Sweep (15/14/13/12/11s): outer-cone slow, extra damage, and a heal for her — this is the anti-heal target. P Adaptive Defenses: physical/magic shield only, true damage ignores it. E Hookshot (16/15/14/13/12s) knocks up and will cancel Meditate. Q Precision Protocol (9/8/7/6/5s) is the auto reset and the true-damage proc.

audit.whatIsWrong: Grievous Wounds is never named in the content layer despite Tactical Sweep being a repeatable heal.
audit.why: Extended fights past first item are your win condition, and her W heal is what stretches them past your DPS.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal named in spikes[2].text, spikes[3].text and late.

edits.before: Your Highlander comes online and lets you contest. Her R (Hextech Ultimatum) traps you in a zone, but you can Q Alpha Strike her E engage and W Meditate to reduce her Q true damage during the trade.
edits.after: Highlander (85s) comes online and lets you contest. The Hextech Ultimatum (R, 140s at rank 1) anchors you to its zone — Alpha Strike blanks her burst window inside it, but never Meditate under her E knockup.

edits.before: With Wuju Style and Berserker's you out-DPS her in a stuck fight — your true damage beats her shielding when you're on her. Bait her E, dodge it with Q, then commit through her W shield.
edits.after: With Wuju Style and Berserker's you out-DPS her in a stuck fight — true damage passes straight through Adaptive Defenses. Bait Hookshot (E, 16s at rank 1), then commit while it is down with anti-heal up.

edits.before: Camille flips it back: her E-R engage locks you in place and her W (Tactical Sweep) true-damage sweep plus her adaptive shield let her burst and peel. If she's ahead she picks you before you stick, so respect her engage and buy a defensive answer.
edits.after: Camille flips it back: her E-R engage locks you in place, and Tactical Sweep (W, 15s) slows and heals her off the outer cone. Adaptive Defenses shields physical or magic only, so your true damage still lands — bring Grievous Wounds, not just resists.

edits.before: Late Camille swings back — her E-R lock and W true-damage shield let her pick and peel, so respect her engage and answer it with a defensive item.
edits.after: Late Camille swings back — her E-R lock picks you off and Tactical Sweep heals her back up, so carry Grievous Wounds and respect the Hookshot angle.

edits.before: Late her E-R lockdown and true-damage shield let her pick and peel you.
edits.after: Late her E-R lockdown and W heal let her pick you off and peel away.

edits.before: Use R to trap you and W shield to survive your DPS
edits.after: Use R to anchor you and W's heal to outlast your DPS

edits.before: Meditate to shrug off her Q enhanced true-damage hit
edits.after: Meditate only after her Hookshot knockup is spent

notes: Two corrections carried over from the mirror: Tactical Sweep is a heal, not true damage, and Adaptive Defenses cannot block true damage, so the 'true-damage shield' framing that appeared three times is removed. The full layer's report[5].t and phases[6].why still reference her 'E shield' and 'true-damage scaling' and should be swept in a later pass — they were left alone here rather than guessed at. Not verifiable from the kits and therefore not written: whether Alpha Strike's untargetability breaks The Hextech Ultimatum's anchor or merely dodges damage inside it.
